A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniComp study. Their complete main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison across the section moves and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original UniComp benchmark results, component ablations, latency measurements, compression analyses and qualitative outputs.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds representation comparisons, temporal-grouping comparisons and detailed latency measurements in supplementary Sections 9–11.

M1.justification: The FGF, TA and SDC procedures, equations and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The new appendix comparisons test alternative representations and grouping strategies without replacing the proposed pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use LongVideoBench, EgoSchema, MLVU and VideoMME, retaining the long-video settings and qualitative question-answering and captioning examples. Adding VideoMME to Table 7's caption identifies the existing experiment's source rather than adding coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds comparisons against Dyseg (FastVid) and Redundancy-Aware (HoliTom) grouping in Table 12. Table 11 also adds VisionZip and HoliTom to the latency comparison, previously shown only for UniComp and full-token inference. Original benchmark comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: New experiments vary SDC representations and temporal grouping choices, and separately profile FGF, TA, SDC and other costs across 32–320 frames. Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. Tables 9 and 12 do not fully specify their model, frame-count and retention settings.

E4.justification: v2 adds targeted analyses of keys versus values/final-layer features (Table 9), alternative temporal grouping strategies (Table 12), and component latency costs (Table 10). These extend the existing module ablations, sensitivity analyses and case studies, which are retained.

E5.justification: Benchmark and timing comparisons continue to report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing compression-distribution plots and their reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 9–12 add representation/grouping scores and detailed timing entries; Tables 1–8 retain their scores. Figure 5 revises the 256-frame vision-tower times from 2525/2455 ms for UniComp/full tokens to 2490/2490 ms, changing the reported speedup from 3.73× to 3.77×.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Gaussian assumption, reconstruction-error argument and supplementary derivation in Equations 1–23 are unchanged. Removing 'Appendix A' from the derivation's heading is cosmetic.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about uniqueness-driven compression, three cooperating modules, minimal configuration requirements, transferability and superior compression performance. The new experiments support existing contributions.

C2.justification: New Sections 10–11 interpret runtime bottlenecks and explain motion preservation through first-frame anchoring and adaptive allocation. Section 10 also introduces an overbroad lower-overhead claim: Table 11 reports 927 ms for UniComp compression versus 474 ms for VisionZip.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies VideoMME as Table 7's dataset and defines Table 1's 'Acc.' as the ratio to the baseline. Hardware, thresholds, evaluation tooling and the code link are unchanged; the implementation paragraph moves from Section 9 to Section 12.

R1.justification: v2 adds Video Compression Commander to Section 2.1 and the bibliography without evaluating it. Other reference changes primarily update publication metadata or numbering; the paper's positioning around information uniqueness remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 inserts short supplementary Sections 9–11, moves and renumbers Implementation Details and Qualitative Examples to Sections 12–13, simplifies the derivation heading and adds author contact notes. Most existing prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: Four appendix tables are added, combining new diagnostics with some previously reported aggregate timings and scores, and locally reflowing pages 10–11. Figure 1 is slightly resized and repositioned, and Tables 1 and 7 receive caption clarifications. The qualitative-example pages are identical.

improvement.justification: The added representation and grouping comparisons and component latency breakdown modestly strengthen empirical support and transparency beyond v1. The gain is limited by incomplete settings for the new ablations and the inaccurate blanket overhead claim in Section 10, contradicted by Table 11's UniComp-versus-VisionZip timings.
